governingRules: Documentation/end vision anchors the graph; implementation is a later evidence projection.
A graph node never upgrades maturity.
Consequential relations require reason and/or evidence.
Current and target dependencies are separate; unknown is represented explicitly rather than inferred.
Legacy is evidence/history, not destination authority.
One semantic node may have many source/evidence/view references.

statusField.description: Status preserves the source-native state/maturity vocabulary where a node originates in a canonical inventory (notably responsibility status). The epistemicStatuses list is the graph-level subset and must not be used as a closed enum for every node kind.

statusRules: document, vision_anchor, destination_concept, journey, requirement, vertical_slice, si_atom, evidence, workstream, reference_piece and composition use graph-epistemic statuses where applicable.
responsibility nodes preserve the canonical responsibility-matrix current-status vocabulary verbatim; that vocabulary is evidence about maturity/placement, not a new graph epistemic class.
Validators must reject missing/non-string status, not unfamiliar source-native status values.

relationSemantics.DEPENDS_ON: A destination/product dependency. In journey mapping this means the journey exercises the responsibility; it is not automatically a hard runtime prerequisite.
relationSemantics.TESTS: A proof/build relation: a candidate composition or vertical slice exercises/tests the connected journey or outcome boundary.
relationSemantics.PROJECTS: A derived projection from the dependency scorecard into the graph; not itself authority over the projected dependency.
relationSemantics.EVIDENCES: Evidence node materially supports the target System Intelligence claim or graph assertion.
